__
 
• **Drik Panchang**

 
 
• Drik Panchang is a comprehensive online Hindu almanac that provides detailed astrological and calendar-related information.
 
• It is used to determine auspicious dates and times for various Hindu religious practices and rituals.
 
• Drik Panchang includes data on festivals, vrat (fasting) dates, and other important Hindu events.
 
• It uses precise astronomical calculations to provide daily panchang details like tithi (lunar day), nakshatra (constellation), yoga, karana, and vara (weekday).
 
• The platform also offers tools to calculate muhurat (auspicious time) for various ceremonies like weddings and housewarming events.
 
• Drik Panchang covers multiple Hindu calendars such as the Vikram Samvat and Shaka Samvat.
 
• The website and app are available in multiple languages to cater to a wide audience.
 
• It also includes predictive astrology features like horoscopes and horoscope matching for marriage.
 
• The panchang is updated regularly to reflect accurate sunrise, sunset, moonrise, and moonset times for different locations.
 
• Drik Panchang is widely used by Hindus around the world for both religious and everyday planning.

• **Maha Shivaratri**

 
 
• Maha Shivaratri is a major Hindu festival dedicated to Lord Shiva, one of the primary deities in Hinduism.
 
• It is celebrated annually on the 14th night of the new moon during the waning phase in the Hindu month of Phalguna or Magha, which typically falls in February or March.
 
• The festival is marked by ritualistic fasting, night-long vigils, and the chanting of Shiva mantras. Devotees visit Shiva temples to perform special pujas and offer milk, honey, and bilva (bael) leaves to the Shiva Lingam.
 
• Maha Shivaratri is believed to be the day when Shiva married Parvati or performed the Tandava, a cosmic dance of creation, preservation, and destruction. It is considered highly auspicious for spiritual growth, attracting devotees seeking the blessings for longevity and prosperity.
 
• The festival emphasizes self-restraint, meditation, and the purification of the mind and soul.

__
 
• **Governor**

 
 
• In India, the governor of a state holds office at the pleasure of the president, which means that the president can remove the governor from office at any time without assigning any reason.
 
• This power is vested in the president under Article 156(1) of the Constitution of India.
 
• The president is advised by the Council of Ministers, which is headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• In practice, this means that the decision to remove a governor is usually taken by the central government, led by the Prime Minister.
 
• There are a number of reasons why the central government might want to remove a governor. These could include:
 
• If the governor is acting in a way that is considered to be unconstitutional or illegal.
 
• If the governor is not fulfilling their constitutional duties, such as providing assents to bills passed by the state legislature.
 
• If the governor is not acting in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• If the governor is acting in a way that is considered to be detrimental to the interests of the state or the country.
 
• However, the central government is unlikely to remove a governor without a clear and compelling reason. This is because removing a governor is a serious matter that can damage the relationship between the central government and the state government.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deputy Speaker**

 
 
• The Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha is the second-highest legislative officer of the Lok Sabha.
 
• Article 93 of the Constitution provides for the election of both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker.
 
• The Lok Sabha has not had a Deputy Speaker for the last 16 months. Instead, a panel of MPs has been assisting the Speaker.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister**
 
 
• Chief Minister is the real executive authority i.e., de facto executive.
 
• The Constitution does not contain any specific procedure for the selection and appointment of the Chief Minister.
 
• Article 164 only says that the Chief Minister shall be appointed by the governor.
 
• The governor has to appoint the leader of the majority party in the state legislative assembly as the Chief Minister.
 
• But, when no party has a clear majority in the assembly, then the governor may exercise his personal discretion and then ask him to prove the majority within a reasonable period.
 
 
 
• **Speaker**
 
 
• Article 93 deals with the appointment of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker.
 
• The inaugural holder of the office of the Lok Sabha was M. A. Ayyangar.
 
• The term length of the deputy speaker of the Lok Sabha is five years during the term of the Lok Sabha.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Palakkad Fort**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Palakkad Fort:**

 
 
• Palakkad Fort, also known as Tipu's Fort, is situated in the state of Kerala.
 
• It was originally built in 1766 by Hyder Ali, the ruler of Mysore. The fort is known for its well-preserved architecture and is constructed primarily from granite.
 
• It played a significant role during the Mysore Wars, witnessing several battles between the British and Mysorean forces.
 
• Today, the fort is maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India and serves as a popular tourist attraction, showcasing Kerala's historical legacy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kittur Fort:**

 
 
• Kittur Fort is located in the Belagavi district in the state of Karnataka.
 
• It was constructed in the early 18th century by Allappa Gowda Sardesai.
 
• The fort is historically significant for its association with Rani Chennamma, who led a famous rebellion against the British East India Company in 1824.
 
• The fort complex includes a palace, a museum, and a memorial dedicated to the valiant queen. Kittur Fort stands as a symbol of resistance and valor in Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Hoysaleswara Temple:**
 
 
• Hoysaleswara Temple is located in Halebidu, which is in the state of Karnataka.
 
• It was built in the 12th century under the patronage of King Vishnuvardhana of the Hoysala Empire.
 
• The temple is renowned for its intricate sculptures and detailed architectural designs, characteristic of Hoysala artistry.
 
• Dedicated to Lord Shiva, the temple complex features two large shrines and a wealth of ornate carvings depicting various Hindu deities and mythological stories.
 
• Hoysaleswara Temple is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and attracts many visitors interested in art and history.
 
 
 
• **Gol Gumbaz: **
 
 
• Gol Gumbaz is situated in the city of Bijapur, in the state of Karnataka.
 
• The mausoleum was constructed in 1656 and serves as the resting place of Sultan Mohammed Adil Shah of the Bijapur Sultanate.
 
• Famous for its massive dome, which is the second-largest in the world, Gol Gumbaz is an outstanding example of Indo-Islamic architecture.
 
• The tomb is specifically noted for its "Whispering Gallery," where even the slightest sound is echoed multiple times.
 
• It remains a significant historical monument and a popular tourist attraction in Karnataka.

questions.question: The Indian Parliament approved the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002, which establishes the fundamental right to elementary education for children aged ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 - 14 Years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act was passed by the Parliament of India in December 2002, and it came into effect on July 1, 2003.
 
• This amendment inserted Article 21A in the Constitution, making education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• It made it mandatory for the State to provide free and compulsory education to all children in this age group.
 
• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, was enacted to operationalize this constitutional mandate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Constitutional Amendment:

 
 
• A constitutional amendment is a change made to the Constitution of a country, which requires a specific procedure to be followed for its adoption.
 
• In India, a constitutional amendment requires a special majority in both houses of Parliament and, in certain cases, ratification by at least half of the state legislatures.
 
 
 
• Article 21A:
 
 
• Article 21A was added to the Indian Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act.
 
• It stipulates that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years in a manner determined by law.
 
 
 
• Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009:
 
 
• The RTE Act was enacted to give effect to Article 21A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It mandates that every child has a right to full-time elementary education of satisfactory and equitable quality in a formal school which satisfies certain essential norms and standards.
 
• It also lays down the responsibilities of the State, parents, schools, and teachers to ensure the implementation of this right.
 
 
 
• Impact of the Amendment:
 
 
• This amendment has significantly increased the enrollment rates in primary schools across India.
 
• It has also brought attention to issues such as infrastructure, quality of education, and teacher training in the Indian educational system.

The correct answer is __**MRTP Act**__.

__
 
• The Monopolistic and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969, was enacted
 
 
• To ensure that the operation of the economic system does not result in the concentration of economic power in hands of a few.
 
• To provide for the control of monopolies.
 
• To prohibit monopolistic and restrictive trade practices.
 
 
 
• The Competition Act was passed in 2002 and has been amended by the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2007.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** FEMA Act **

 
 
• Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) which was passed in the year 1999, replaced the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973.
 
• The purpose of FEMA is to consolidate and amend the law related to foreign exchange for facilitating external trade and payment in an orderly manner and also to develops a foreign exchange market in India.
 
• FEMA is applicable to all parts of India. The act is also applicable to all branches, offices, and agencies outside India owned or controlled by a person who is a resident of India.
 
• The FEMA head-office, also known as Enforcement Directorate is situated in New Delhi and is headed by a Director.
 
 

 

 
• Industrial Policy Act 1991:
 
 
• The government controls trade restrictions through various measures and policies, including the Industrial Policy Act 1991.
 
• The Industrial Policy Act of 1991 was a significant policy reform introduced by the Indian government to liberalize and deregulate the industrial sector.
 
• It aimed to promote competition, attract foreign investment, and facilitate trade by removing unnecessary restrictions and barriers.
 
• Under the Industrial Policy Act 1991, the government implemented several measures to liberalize trade, such as reducing import tariffs, relaxing licensing requirements, promoting foreign direct investment, and encouraging technological advancements.
 
• These reforms helped in opening up the Indian economy, expanding trade opportunities, and integrating India into the global market.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Trade Policy **
 
 
• The tenure of the foreign trade policy is 5 years and its license renewed annually.
 
• The FTP is updated every year on the 31st of March and the modifications, improvements and new schemes become effective from 1st April of every year.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution is related with right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases?

__
 
• **Article 41: **

 
 
• Article 41 of the Indian Constitution mandates that the state shall make effective provisions for securing the right to work, education, and public assistance in cases such as unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement within its economic capacity.
 
• This article falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• It emphasizes social security and welfare for citizens. Although not legally enforceable, it provides a guiding framework for state policies.

• Article 44 directs the state to strive to secure a Uniform Civil Code for all citizens throughout India.
 
• This article is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• It aims to establish common personal laws irrespective of religion.
 
• The goal is national integration and equal treatment under the law.
 
 
 
• **Article 43: **
 
 
• Article 43 calls on the state to endeavor to secure a living wage, decent working conditions, and social and cultural opportunities for all workers.
 
• It is included in the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• The article highlights the importance of workers' welfare and quality of life.
 
• It serves as a guideline for labor policies, though it is not enforceable by law.
 
 
 
• **Article 42: **
 
 
• Article 42 directs the state to make provisions for just and humane working conditions and maternity relief.
 
• This article is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• It underscores the importance of protecting the health and rights of workers, especially women.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of igneous rock?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rhyolite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__Classification of Rocks__

 
• Igneous Rocks

 
 
• Igneous rocks are crystalline solids that form directly from the cooling of magma.
 
• This is an exothermic process (it loses heat) and involves a phase change from the liquid to the solid-state.
 
• Igneous rocks are given names based upon two things: composition (what they are made of) and texture (how big the crystals are)
 
• Intrusive igneous rocks crystallize below Earth's surface, and the slow cooling that occurs there allows large crystals to form.
 
• Examples: diorite, gabbro, granite, pegmatite, and peridotite.
 
• Extrusive igneous rocks erupt onto the surface, where they cool quickly to form small crystals.
 
• Some cool so quickly that they form an amorphous glass.
 
• Examples: andesite, basalt, dacite, obsidian, pumice, rhyolite, scoria, and tuff.
 
 
 
• Sedimentary rocks
 
 
• Sedimentary rocks are formed by the accumulation of sediments
 
• They are formed by
 
 
• Weathering (breccia, conglomerate, sandstone, siltstone, and shale)
 
• Can form when dissolved material precipitate from solution (Rock salt, iron ore, chert, flint, some dolomites, and some limestones)
 
• Accumulation of plant or animal debris (coal, some dolomites, and some limestones)
 
 
 
 
 
• Metamorphic rocks
 
 
• Metamorphic rocks have been modified by heat, pressure, and chemical processes, usually while buried deep below Earth's surface.
 
• Exposure to these extreme conditions has altered the mineralogy, texture, and chemical composition of the rocks.
 
• Example: gneiss, phyllite, schist, and slate, Marble, etc.

questions.question: It is a Fundamental Duty of parents to provide educational opportunities to wards aged ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 - 14 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• It is a Fundamental Duty of every parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the age of **6 and 14 years**.
 
• This duty is outlined under **Article 51A(k)** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The **Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009**, also mandates free and compulsory education for children in this age group.
 
• The RTE Act stipulates that every child has a right to full-time elementary education of satisfactory and equitable quality in a formal school which satisfies certain essential norms and standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties are a set of obligations that every Indian citizen is expected to perform to contribute to the welfare of the country and uphold its unity and integrity.
 
• They were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A**
 
 
• Article 51A of the Indian Constitution specifies the Fundamental Duties of citizens.
 
• These duties include respecting the Constitution, the national flag and the national anthem, promoting harmony, protecting the environment, and providing educational opportunities to children, among others.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009**
 
 
• The RTE Act, 2009, aims to provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• The Act makes it obligatory on the part of the government to ensure that every child gets free elementary education.
 
• It also lays down the norms and standards related to pupil-teacher ratios, buildings and infrastructure, school-working days, teacher-working hours, etc.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs regarding the judicial powers of the Indian President and their definition is INCORRECTLY matched?

options.text: Commutation – It denotes the substitution of one form of punishment for a lighter form
Respite – It denotes awarding a lesser sentence in place of that which was originally awarded
Reprieve – It implies reducing the period of sentence without changing its character
Pardon – it removes both the sentences and the conviction

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reprieve – It implies reducing the period of sentence without changing its character**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Commutation – It denotes the substitution of one form of punishment for a lighter form.
 
• Respite – It denotes awarding a lesser sentence in place of that which was originally awarded.
 
• Reprieve – It implies a temporary stay of the execution of a sentence, especially of death.
 
• Pardon – It removes both the sentences and the conviction, freeing the person from all legal penalties and disabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Commutation:**

 
 
• This power allows the President to reduce the severity of a punishment or sentence. For example, a death sentence may be commuted to life imprisonment.
 
 
 
• **Respite:**
 
 
• This is the award of a lesser sentence due to special circumstances such as the physical disability of the convict or the pregnancy of a woman offender.
 
 
 
• **Reprieve:**
 
 
• A reprieve is a temporary delay of punishment, especially a death sentence.
 
• It is typically granted to allow the convict more time to seek a pardon or some other form of clemency.
 
 
 
• **Pardon:**
 
 
• A pardon completely absolves the person of the crime and the conviction, effectively erasing all legal consequences of the offense.
 
• It is an act of clemency that forgives the convict and releases them from further punishment.

questions.question: Which of the following is an RBI-registered NBFC- MFI that works on a Joint Liability Group lending model of Grameen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fusion Microfinance Pvt Ltd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Fusion Microfinance Pvt Ltd** is an RBI-registered NBFC-MFI that focuses on providing financial services to underserved women in India.
 
• It operates on the Joint Liability Group (JLG) lending model of Grameen, which enables group borrowing and ensures better repayment rates.
 
• The company aims to empower women entrepreneurs by providing them with easy access to credit for their small businesses.
 
• Fusion Microfinance Pvt Ltd has a presence in multiple states across India, ensuring a wide reach and impact on improving financial inclusion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC)**

 
 
• An NBFC is a financial institution that provides banking services without meeting the legal definition of a bank.
 
• NBFCs are involved in various financial activities, including loans and credit facilities, retirement planning, money markets, underwriting, and merger activities.
 
• They are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) under the RBI Act, 1934.
 
 
 
• **Microfinance Institution (MFI)**
 
 
• Microfinance Institutions are organizations that provide financial services to low-income individuals or those who do not have access to typical banking services.
 
• MFIs aim to promote financial inclusion by offering small loans, savings, insurance, and other basic financial products.
 
• These institutions play a crucial role in empowering economically disadvantaged communities and fostering entrepreneurship.
 
 
 
• **Joint Liability Group (JLG) Model**
 
 
• The JLG model is a lending methodology where a small group of individuals (usually women) come together to borrow from a bank or financial institution.
 
• All group members guarantee each other's loans, thus reducing the risk of default and ensuring better credit discipline.
 
• This model is particularly effective in microfinance, where traditional collateral is not available.
 
 
 
• **Grameen Model**
 
 
• The Grameen model of microfinance was pioneered by Nobel Laureate Muhammad Yunus in Bangladesh.
 
• It focuses on providing small loans to the impoverished without requiring collateral.
 
• The model emphasizes trust and social capital, where peer pressure within groups ensures high repayment rates.

questions.question: Annie Besant was a Fabian socialist under the influence of _________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**George Bernard Shaw**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Annie Besant was a British socialist, theosophist, women's rights activist, writer, orator, educationist, and philanthropist.
 
• She was a prominent figure in the Fabian Society, a socialist organization in the United Kingdom.
 
• George Bernard Shaw, an Irish playwright and critic, was one of the founding members of the Fabian Society and had a significant influence on Annie Besant.
 
• The Fabian Society aimed at the establishment of a democratic socialist state in the United Kingdom through gradual and reformist means.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fabian Society**

 
 
• Established in 1884, the Fabian Society is a British socialist organization that aimed to advance the principles of democratic socialism via gradualist and reformist efforts rather than revolutionary means.
 
• It is associated with the Labour Party in the UK and was instrumental in the party's formation.
 
• The society's members, known as Fabians, have included prominent figures such as George Bernard Shaw, H.G. Wells, and Sidney and Beatrice Webb.
 
• The society's influence extended into the fields of politics, education, and social reform.
 
 
 
• **George Bernard Shaw**
 
 
• George Bernard Shaw (1856-1950) was an Irish playwright, critic, polemicist, and political activist.
 
• He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1925 and is best known for his plays, including "Pygmalion" and "Man and Superman."
 
• Shaw was a co-founder of the London School of Economics and a member of the Fabian Society, where he advocated for gradual social reform and the establishment of a welfare state.
 
• His works and ideas had a significant influence on contemporary social and political thought.
 
 
 
• **Annie Besant**
 
 
• Annie Besant (1847-1933) was a prominent British socialist, theosophist, women's rights activist, writer, and orator.
 
• She became involved in the Indian independence movement and served as the president of the Indian National Congress in 1917.
 
• Besant was also influential in the Theosophical Society, where she worked to promote spiritual and educational reforms.
 
• Her contributions to social reform, education, and the fight for Indian independence remain significant in history.

questions.question: Ibn Battuta’s book of travels, called Rihla was originally written in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arabic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ibn Battuta** was a Moroccan scholar and explorer who is widely recognized for his extensive travels.
 
• **Rihla** is the name of his travelogue, which translates to "The Journey" in Arabic.
 
• Ibn Battuta's Rihla was **originally written in Arabic**, the scholarly and literary language of the Islamic world at that time.
 
• The Rihla provides a detailed account of his travels, covering about 75,000 miles across the Islamic world and beyond.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ibn Battuta**

 
 
• Born in 1304 in Tangier, Morocco, Ibn Battuta was one of the greatest travelers of the medieval world.
 
• His journeys lasted for almost 30 years, covering North Africa, the Horn of Africa, West Africa, Southern Europe, Eastern Europe, the Middle East, South Asia, Central Asia, Southeast Asia, and China.
 
• His travels were initially motivated by the desire to go on the Hajj, the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca.
 
• He visited many of the known Islamic lands and beyond, making observations on the cultures, people, governance, and practices of the regions he traveled.
 
 
 
• **Rihla**
 
 
• The term "Rihla" means journey in Arabic and refers to a genre of Arabic literature that details a journey or series of journeys.
 
• Ibn Battuta's Rihla is one of the most famous works of this genre.
 
• The Rihla of Ibn Battuta was compiled from his travel notes and dictated to a scholar named Ibn Juzayy in the court of Sultan Abu Inan Faris.
 
• This travelogue is a valuable historical document, providing insight into the medieval Islamic world and the various cultures Ibn Battuta encountered.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Arabic**
 
 
• During Ibn Battuta's time, Arabic was the lingua franca of the Islamic world.
 
• It was the language of scholarship, science, literature, and governance.
 
• Arabic enabled scholars and travelers to communicate and share knowledge across vast distances within the Islamic empire.
 
• The use of Arabic for the Rihla made the work accessible to a wide audience within the Islamic world and ensured its preservation and influence.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution states that no citizen of India shall accept any title from any foreign State?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 18 (2)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 18 of the Indian Constitution pertains to the abolition of titles.
 
• Clause (2) of Article 18 states that no citizen of India shall accept any title from any foreign State.
 
• This provision is meant to ensure that Indian citizens do not owe allegiance to any foreign power through the acceptance of titles.
 
• Article 18 in its entirety is aimed at abolishing the practice of conferring titles that create artificial social hierarchies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 18 (1)**

 
 
• No title, not being a military or academic distinction, shall be conferred by the State.
 
• This clause prohibits the Indian government from conferring any titles that are not related to military or academic achievements.
 
 
 
• **Article 18 (3)**
 
 
• No person who is not a citizen of India shall, while he holds any office of profit or trust under the State, accept without the consent of the President any title from any foreign State.
 
• This clause restricts non-citizens holding office under the Indian State from accepting titles from foreign states without presidential consent.
 
 
 
• **Article 18 (4)**
 
 
• No person holding any office of profit or trust under the State shall, without the consent of the President, accept any present, emolument, or office of any kind from or under any foreign State.
 
• This clause prohibits persons holding office under the Indian State from accepting any form of present, emolument, or office from foreign states without presidential consent.

questions.question: Anantha R Krishnan is a famous _________ player.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mridangam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Anantha R Krishnan is a renowned mridangam player known for his exceptional skill and contribution to Carnatic music.
 
• He is recognized for his innovative techniques and has collaborated with many eminent musicians globally.
 
• Anantha R Krishnan has performed in several prestigious music festivals and has received numerous accolades for his performances.
 
• He comes from a family of legendary mridangam players, further enriching his understanding and mastery of the instrument.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mridangam**

 
 
• The mridangam is a percussion instrument from South India and is a primary rhythmic accompaniment in Carnatic music performances.
 
• It is a double-headed drum made of wood, with the two drumheads being made of animal skin. The right head (valanthalai) produces a higher pitch while the left head (edanthalai) produces a lower pitch.
 
• Playing the mridangam involves complex finger and hand techniques, requiring years of practice to master the intricate rhythms and patterns.
 
• The mridangam has a rich history, being mentioned in ancient Indian texts and sculptures, and remains a vital part of Indian classical music traditions.
 
 
 
• **Flute**
 
 
• The flute is a woodwind instrument without reeds, producing sound from the flow of air across an opening.
 
• In Indian classical music, the bamboo flute, known as bansuri in the North and venu in the South, is widely used.
 
• The flute has a significant presence in various musical traditions globally, from classical to folk music.
 
 
 
• **Santoor**
 
 
• The santoor is a trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer, originating from the Indian subcontinent, particularly used in Kashmiri and Hindustani music.
 
• It has a set of strings stretched over a wooden box, and the sound is produced by striking the strings with a pair of mallets.
 
• The santoor is known for its rich, resonant sound and is often used in classical Indian compositions.
 
 
 
• **Sitar**
 
 
• The sitar is a plucked string instrument used in Hindustani classical music, known for its distinctive sound and complex playing techniques.
 
• It has a long neck with movable frets and sympathetic strings that resonate with the played strings, adding to its rich tonal quality.
 
• The sitar became globally popular in the 20th century, especially through the works of maestros like Ravi Shankar.

questions.question: Prior to India, which country introduced Five-Year Plans for policy-making purposes?

options.text: The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) was the first country to introduce the concept of Five-Year Plans.
 
• The USSR introduced its first Five-Year Plan in 1928 under the leadership of Joseph Stalin.
 
• The primary goal of the first Five-Year Plan was to rapidly industrialize the nation and boost its economy.
 
• The success of the Soviet Five-Year Plans influenced many other countries, including India, to adopt similar planning strategies for economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans**

 
 
• Five-Year Plans are centralized and integrated national economic programs.
 
• The concept was first implemented in the Soviet Union and later adopted by various other countries.
 
• These plans aim to develop sectors such as agriculture, industry, and services by setting specific targets over a five-year period.
 
• The plans are designed to achieve rapid economic development and are often associated with socialist and centrally planned economies.
 
 
 
• **Soviet Five-Year Plans**
 
 
• The first Soviet Five-Year Plan (1928-1932) focused on the rapid industrialization of the USSR, particularly in heavy industries such as steel, coal, and machinery.
 
• The plan also aimed to collectivize agriculture to increase productivity and ensure state control over food supplies.
 
• Despite initial challenges and resistance, the first plan achieved significant industrial growth and laid the foundation for future economic development.
 
• Subsequent Five-Year Plans continued to build on these achievements, with varying degrees of success and challenges.
 
 
 
• **India's Five-Year Plans**
 
 
• India adopted the concept of Five-Year Plans after gaining independence in 1947.
 
• The Planning Commission was established in 1950 to oversee the formulation and implementation of these plans.
 
• India's first Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) focused on agriculture, irrigation, and energy production to rebuild the economy after independence.
 
• India continued to implement Five-Year Plans until the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015.

questions.question: The Great Bath in Mohenjo-Daro was excavated in which of the following areas?

__
 
• The Great Bath is one of the most famous and well-preserved structures of the ancient city of Mohenjo-Daro.
 
• It was discovered in the Citadel area of Mohenjo-Daro, indicating its significance in the urban planning of the city.
 
• The Citadel was a fortified area that contained important buildings and structures, likely used for administrative and religious purposes.
 
• The Great Bath measures approximately 12 meters long, 7 meters wide, and 2.4 meters deep, and it was likely used for ritual bathing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohenjo-Daro:**

 
 
• Mohenjo-Daro is one of the largest settlements of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization, located in present-day Pakistan.
 
• The name Mohenjo-Daro means "Mound of the Dead Men" in Sindhi.
 
• The city was built around 2500 BCE and was one of the world's earliest major urban centers.
 
• The site was rediscovered in the 1920s by archaeologists Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay and John Marshall.
 
 
 
• **Indus Valley Civilization:**
 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization (IVC) was a Bronze Age civilization that flourished in the northwestern regions of South Asia, including present-day Pakistan and northwest India.
 
• It is also known as the Harappan Civilization, named after the first discovered site, Harappa.
 
• The IVC is noted for its advanced urban planning, architecture, and social organization.
 
• Key features of the IVC include well-planned cities, sophisticated drainage systems, and the use of standardized weights and measures.
 
 
 
• **Citadel:**
 
 
• The Citadel was a raised area in the city, typically fortified, and contained important structures such as granaries, public baths, and assembly halls.
 
• The elevated platform of the Citadel provided protection from floods and attacks.
 
• It was likely the center of administration and religious activities in the city.
 
 
 
• **Ritual Bathing:**
 
 
• Ritual bathing was an important practice in many ancient civilizations, often associated with religious and ceremonial activities.
 
• The Great Bath of Mohenjo-Daro is one of the earliest examples of a large, public water tank used for such purposes.
 
• The meticulous construction and waterproofing of the Great Bath suggest its significance in the cultural and religious life of the inhabitants.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is/are correct about cropland ecosystem?

**Statement 1.** Cropland is a man-made ecosystem.

**Statement 2.** Very less genetic diversity is found in cropland ecosystem.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both statements 1 and 2 correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Statement 1: Cropland is indeed a man-made ecosystem created by human activities for the purpose of agriculture.
 
• Statement 2: Cropland ecosystems generally have very low genetic diversity because they are typically monocultures or limited to a few crop species.
 
• Croplands are heavily managed environments, often involving activities such as plowing, planting, irrigation, and the application of fertilizers and pesticides.
 
• These ecosystems are designed to maximize the production of specific crops, leading to reduced biodiversity compared to natural ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Man-made Ecosystems**

 
 
• Man-made ecosystems, also known as artificial or anthropogenic ecosystems, are created and maintained by humans.
 
 
• **Genetic Diversity**
 
 
• Genetic diversity refers to the total number of genetic characteristics in the genetic makeup of a species.
 
• It is essential for the adaptability and survival of species, as it allows populations to adapt to changing environmental conditions.
 
• In croplands, genetic diversity is often low because farmers typically grow a limited number of high-yield crop varieties.
 
 
 
• **Monoculture**
 
 
• Monoculture is the agricultural practice of growing a single crop species over a large area for a consecutive number of years.
 
• While it can increase efficiency and yield, it also makes crops more vulnerable to pests and diseases, which can spread rapidly in genetically uniform populations.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Agriculture**
 
 
• Sustainable agriculture aims to produce food in a way that maintains the health of ecosystems and conserves biodiversity.
 
• Techniques include crop rotation, polyculture, and the use of organic fertilizers and pest control methods.

__
 
• Bharatanatyam is a classical Indian dance form that originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is one of the oldest classical dance traditions in India, with its roots tracing back to the ancient Tamil culture.
 
• Bharatanatyam combines expressive dance (abhinaya) with rhythmic footwork (nritta) to convey religious and mythological stories.
 
• The dance form is typically performed by a solo dancer and is accompanied by Carnatic music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Origin of Bharatanatyam:**

 
 
• Bharatanatyam originated in the Hindu temples of Tamil Nadu and was initially performed by devadasis (temple dancers).
 
• The dance form's history can be traced back to the Natya Shastra, an ancient treatise on performing arts written by the sage Bharata.
 
• It was later codified and standardized in the 19th and 20th centuries by notable dance gurus such as Rukmini Devi Arundale and E. Krishna Iyer.
 
 
 
• **Structure of a Bharatanatyam Performance:**
 
 
• A typical Bharatanatyam performance consists of a series of dances, including Alarippu (invocation), Jatiswaram (pure dance), Shabdam (expressive dance), Varnam (narrative dance), Padams (lyrical dance), and Tillana (concluding dance).
 
• Each segment showcases the dancer's technical prowess, emotional expression, and storytelling ability.
 
 
 
• **Costume and Makeup:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam dancers wear traditional costumes, usually consisting of a saree draped in a distinctive style that allows for freedom of movement.
 
• The makeup includes intricate facial designs, expressive eye makeup, and jewelry that enhances the dancer's expressions and movements.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Bharatanatyam:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is not just a dance form but a spiritual practice that conveys stories from Hindu mythology and religious themes.
 
• It plays a crucial role in preserving and promoting Indian cultural heritage and is performed at various cultural festivals and events worldwide.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a noble gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitrogen (N)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nitrogen (N) is not a noble gas**; it is a diatomic molecule in its natural form and makes up around 78% of the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• **Noble gases** are a group of chemical elements with similar properties under standard conditions: they are all odorless, colorless, monatomic gases with very low chemical reactivity.
 
• **Argon (Ar), Neon (Ne), and Helium (He)** are all noble gases, belonging to Group 18 of the periodic table, also known as the noble gas group.
 
• Nitrogen is located in Group 15 of the periodic table and is known for forming strong triple bonds in diatomic N₂ molecules, contributing to its inertness under normal conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Noble Gases**

 
 
• Noble gases include Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenon (Xe), and Radon (Rn).
 
• They are characterized by their full valence electron shell, which makes them very stable and unreactive.
 
• They are used in various applications such as lighting (Neon lights), welding (Argon), and even in medical fields (Helium for respiratory treatments).
 
• Due to their inert nature, they do not easily form compounds, making them useful in environments where reactions are undesirable.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen**
 
 
• Nitrogen is a non-metal element with the symbol N and atomic number 7.
 
• It is essential for life, being a critical component of amino acids and nucleic acids (DNA and RNA).
 
• Nitrogen is largely inert due to the strong triple bond in N₂ molecules, requiring high energy to break.
 
• It is used in various industrial processes, including the production of ammonia for fertilizers through the Haber process.

questions.question: National income at current prices are calculated based on _________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**prevailing prices**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• National income at current prices is calculated based on the **current or prevailing prices** in the market during the year of measurement.
 
• It reflects the **actual monetary value** of goods and services produced in the economy during a given period, without adjusting for inflation.
 
• This method provides a **nominal measure** of national income, which can be higher due to price increases over time.
 
• It is important for understanding the **real-time economic performance** but can be misleading for comparing economic performance over different periods due to the impact of inflation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constant Prices:**

 
 
• This method calculates national income by using the prices of a base year to remove the effects of inflation.
 
• It provides a real measure of national income, allowing for accurate comparisons over different periods.
 
• Constant prices help in understanding the actual growth in the volume of goods and services produced.
 
 
 
• **Future Prices:**
 
 
• Future prices are speculative and not used for calculating current national income.
 
• They are often used in financial markets and economic forecasting to predict future economic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Comparative Prices:**
 
 
• Comparative prices are used to compare the prices of goods and services across different markets or periods.
 
• They help in understanding price differentials and cost competitiveness.

questions.question: According to the census of India 2011, which group of states and union territories from the following recorded the highest literacy rate?

• **Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Yojana (PMGKY)**

 
 
• It aimed to curb black money and bring undisclosed income to the mainstream economy.
 
• Under the scheme, individuals could declare their black money by paying a tax at 30% of the undisclosed income, along with a penalty of 10% and a surcharge of 33% of tax (i.e., 33% of 30%).
 
• The declarant had to deposit 25% of the undisclosed income in the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Deposit Scheme (PMGKDS), which would be interest-free and locked in for four years.
 
• The scheme was a part of the government's efforts to curb tax evasion and increase transparency in the financial system.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)**
 
 
• Launched on 28th August 2014, PMJDY aims to provide universal access to banking facilities.
